title: One Missing Enzyme
endLine: Read adrenal disease in order: enzymes, then receptors, then loops.

scenes.tts: An enzyme beside the kidney's receptor decides which steroid reaches it. Inside the adrenal gland, enzymes decide which steroids get made. Some newborns lack one of those enzymes. Yet one kind of hormone rises. How can losing an enzyme make more hormone?
scenes.narration: An enzyme beside the kidney's receptor decides which steroid reaches it. Inside the adrenal gland, enzymes decide which steroids get made. Some newborns lack one of those enzymes. Yet one kind of hormone rises. How can losing an enzyme make more hormone?
scenes.caption: An enzyme beside the kidney's receptor decides which steroid reaches it. Inside the adrenal gland, enzymes decide which steroids get made. Some newborns lack one of those enzymes. Yet one kind of hormone rises. How can losing an enzyme make more hormone?
scenes.visual: Continue the first film's colour map without a reset. COLOUR BY CONCEPT, as before: aldosterone YELLOW; cortisol PURPLE (filled dots); the mineralocorticoid receptor BLUE; a working enzyme GREEN; an enzyme switched off RED; sodium TEAL; GREY for neutral notes. New in this film: adrenal androgens MAGENTA; ACTH WHITE (thick white arrows from a white-outlined pituitary block); precursors that pile up are HOLLOW PURPLE rings (on the cortisol route, not yet cortisol). A small 'schematic' tag sits at bottom left all film. Opening (link-back): the first film's BLUE receptor with its GREEN guard-enzyme block beside it, at right; a PURPLE cortisol dot turns GREY at the enzyme and a YELLOW aldosterone dot docks. On 'Inside the adrenal gland', the camera pulls left and the receptor shrinks to the lower right corner (it stays all film, labelled 'kidney receptor'). The new world grows on the left 65% of the frame and about 75% of its height: THE STEROID TREE. A thick GREY trunk rises from a base labelled 'cholesterol'; at its top it splits into three branches: left YELLOW ending at 'aldosterone', middle PURPLE ending at 'cortisol', right MAGENTA ending at 'androgens'. Pale dots flow up the trunk and take each branch's colour as they pass small GREEN enzyme gates on the branches. On 'Some newborns lack one', one GREEN gate flickers RED. On 'one kind of hormone rises', the MAGENTA branch tip swells and brightens. Large white question across the top: 'Lose an enzyme, gain a hormone?'

Title 'One Missing Enzyme' fades in above the tree for 2 seconds while the question text fades out. The flickering gate returns to GREEN. Dots keep flowing up the trunk into all three branches at steady rates.

scenes.tts: In the adrenal cortex, steroids grow like a tree. Cholesterol enters one shared trunk, and A C T H speeds that slow first step. Three branches leave it, ending in aldosterone, cortisol and mostly weak androgens. One enzyme, twenty-one hydroxylase, sits on the routes to cortisol and aldosterone. The androgen branch does not need it.
scenes.narration: In the adrenal cortex, steroids grow like a tree. Cholesterol enters one shared trunk, and ACTH speeds that slow first step. Three branches leave it, ending in aldosterone, cortisol and mostly weak androgens. One enzyme, 21-hydroxylase, sits on the routes to cortisol and aldosterone. The androgen branch does not need it.

scenes.visual: Same tree, filling the left 65%. On 'one shared trunk', the GREY trunk glows from base to fork. On 'A C T H', a white-outlined block labelled 'pituitary' appears at top right and a thick WHITE arrow labelled 'ACTH' runs from it to the base of the trunk; the flow of dots up the trunk quickens a little. On 'Three branches', each branch lights in turn with its end label: 'aldosterone' (YELLOW), 'cortisol' (PURPLE), 'androgens' (MAGENTA). On 'twenty-one hydroxylase', a GREEN gate on the YELLOW branch and a GREEN gate on the PURPLE branch pulse together, joined by a thin GREEN bracket labelled '21-hydroxylase'. On 'does not need it', the MAGENTA branch glows: it has no 21-hydroxylase gate. Dots keep flowing through all three branches. Flows are schematic: no amounts.

scenes.tts: Read any adrenal state in three steps, in this order. One, the enzymes: a missing enzyme lowers everything after it, and backs up what comes just before. Two, the receptors: what can the steroids now present do? Three, only then, the loops.
scenes.narration: Read any adrenal state in three steps, in this order. One, the enzymes: a missing enzyme lowers everything after it, and backs up what comes just before. Two, the receptors: what can the steroids now present do? Three, only then, the loops.

scenes.visual: A numbered strip of three large labels builds across the top of the frame, one per spoken step, each pointing at the part of the world it reads: '1 enzymes' with a thin arrow to the GREEN gates on the tree; '2 receptors' with an arrow to the BLUE kidney receptor at lower right; '3 loops' with an arrow to the WHITE pituitary and its ACTH arrow. On 'lowers everything after it', a ghost demonstration on the PURPLE branch only: dots thin out past the gate. On 'backs up what comes just before', a few HOLLOW PURPLE rings gather just before the gate, then the ghost clears. The strip stays at the top, dimmed, for the next four scenes; the active step brightens when it is named.

scenes.tts: Take classic salt-wasting twenty-one hydroxylase deficiency, where enzyme activity is near zero. Step one. Cortisol and aldosterone fall. Seventeen hydroxyprogesterone, the substrate just before the block, piles up. It is the screening marker.
scenes.narration: Take classic salt-wasting 21-hydroxylase deficiency, where enzyme activity is near zero. Step one. Cortisol and aldosterone fall. 17-hydroxyprogesterone, the substrate just before the block, piles up. It is the screening marker.
scenes.caption: Take classic salt-wasting 21-hydroxylase deficiency, where enzyme activity is near zero. Step one. Cortisol and aldosterone fall. 17-hydroxyprogesterone, the substrate just before the block, piles up. It is the screening marker.
scenes.visual: Label '21-hydroxylase deficiency' appears at top left under the strip. Both GREEN 21-hydroxylase gates turn RED and close, each marked with a cross. '1 enzymes' brightens in the strip. On 'Cortisol and aldosterone fall', dots past both RED gates thin to almost none; the 'cortisol' and 'aldosterone' end labels dim. On 'piles up', HOLLOW PURPLE rings crowd in front of the RED gate on the PURPLE branch and keep collecting, labelled '17-OH-progesterone'. On 'screening marker', a small GREY tag 'screening marker' attaches to the pile. Dots still flow up the trunk; the MAGENTA branch carries its usual stream.

scenes.tts: Step two. Nothing that piles up can replace aldosterone, because the block comes before the precursor that acts like aldosterone. Worse, backed-up progesterone and seventeen hydroxyprogesterone weakly block the mineralocorticoid receptor. They can add to the salt loss.
scenes.narration: Step two. Nothing that piles up can replace aldosterone, because the block comes before the precursor that acts like aldosterone. Worse, backed-up progesterone and 17-hydroxyprogesterone weakly block the mineralocorticoid receptor. They can add to the salt loss.

scenes.visual: '2 receptors' brightens in the strip. The BLUE kidney receptor at lower right grows to a readable size (about a quarter of the frame) while the tree stays in place. Its socket is empty: no YELLOW dots arrive. On 'before the precursor', the RED gate on the YELLOW branch pulses, with a short GREY tag 'block before DOC'. On 'weakly block', a few HOLLOW PURPLE rings drift from the pile to the receptor and rest loosely in the socket without lighting it; the receptor stays dim, labelled 'weak blockers'. On 'salt loss', a few TEAL sodium dots slip away from the receptor area downward, labelled 'sodium lost'.

scenes.tts: Step three, the loops. Low cortisol releases the brake on A C T H, which drives the shared trunk harder. The extra flow spills into the one branch still open: the androgens. They rise, and long A C T H drive enlarges the gland. Meanwhile sodium is lost, so volume and pressure fall.
scenes.narration: Step three, the loops. Low cortisol releases the brake on ACTH, which drives the shared trunk harder. The extra flow spills into the one branch still open: the androgens. They rise, and long ACTH drive enlarges the gland. Meanwhile sodium is lost, so volume and pressure fall.

scenes.visual: '3 loops' brightens in the strip; the receptor shrinks back to the lower right corner. A thin PURPLE feedback arrow from the 'cortisol' tip to the pituitary, labelled 'brake', fades to a ghost on 'releases the brake'. The WHITE ACTH arrow thickens and pulses faster, labelled 'ACTH up'. Dots race up the trunk. At the fork, the YELLOW and PURPLE branches stay shut at their RED gates and the PURPLE pile grows; the surplus dots turn MAGENTA and pour into the androgen branch, which swells and brightens, its tip labelled 'androgens up'. On 'enlarges the gland', the whole tree outline widens slightly, tagged 'hyperplasia'. On 'volume and pressure fall', TEAL dots keep slipping away at lower right and a small GREY label 'volume, pressure down' appears with a down arrow. The answer to the opening question is the MAGENTA branch: more hormone from a missing enzyme.

scenes.tts: Now use the rule on two adults who both make too much cortisol. In one, the pituitary makes too much A C T H. In the other, an adrenal adenoma makes cortisol on its own. Which way do the adrenal androgens go in each?
scenes.narration: Now use the rule on two adults who both make too much cortisol. In one, the pituitary makes too much ACTH. In the other, an adrenal adenoma makes cortisol on its own. Which way do the adrenal androgens go in each?
scenes.caption: Now use the rule on two adults who both make too much cortisol. In one, the pituitary makes too much ACTH. In the other, an adrenal adenoma makes cortisol on its own. Which way do the adrenal androgens go in each?
scenes.visual: The deficiency labels, the PURPLE pile and the TEAL dots fade; both RED gates return to GREEN (these adults have the enzyme). The receptor and the strip fade out. The tree, with its pituitary, splits into two half-size copies side by side, filling the frame. Left copy labelled 'too much ACTH': its WHITE ACTH arrow is thick and pulsing. Right copy labelled 'adrenal adenoma': a round PURPLE lump labelled 'adenoma' sits on the cortisol branch, pumping out PURPLE dots. Both cortisol tips glow bright, labelled 'cortisol high'. Both MAGENTA branches are drawn but greyed, each with a large '?' at its tip. Question card at top in white: 'Androgens: up or down?'
Predict pause. The question card stays. Both trees keep a slow flow of dots up their trunks; both cortisol tips glow; the two greyed MAGENTA branches and their '?' marks hold still. No other change.

scenes.tts: With too much A C T H, the whole trunk is driven, so androgens rise with cortisol. The adenoma's cortisol suppresses A C T H. The androgen-making zone goes quiet with it, so androgens fall. Both have high cortisol, yet their androgens move in opposite directions. The difference is step three, the loops.
scenes.narration: With too much ACTH, the whole trunk is driven, so androgens rise with cortisol. The adenoma's cortisol suppresses ACTH. The androgen-making zone goes quiet with it, so androgens fall. Both have high cortisol, yet their androgens move in opposite directions. The difference is step three, the loops.

scenes.visual: Question card dissolves. LEFT tree: on 'the whole trunk is driven', dots race up its trunk under the thick WHITE arrow; its MAGENTA branch fills with colour and brightens, the '?' becoming 'androgens up'. RIGHT tree: on 'suppresses ACTH', a PURPLE feedback arrow runs from the adenoma's cortisol to the pituitary, and the WHITE ACTH arrow thins to a faint dashed line labelled 'ACTH down'. On 'goes quiet', the MAGENTA branch empties and dims, the '?' becoming 'androgens down'; the PURPLE adenoma keeps pumping cortisol. On 'opposite directions', the two MAGENTA tips pulse side by side, one bright, one dim. On 'step three, the loops', both WHITE ACTH arrows glow, labelled 'the loop decides'.

scenes.tts: So start where the pathway breaks. Then ask what the steroids left behind can do. Let the feedback respond last. This rule predicts each level's direction compared with a healthy person, not its size.
scenes.narration: So start where the pathway breaks. Then ask what the steroids left behind can do. Let the feedback respond last. This rule predicts each level's direction compared with a healthy person, not its size.

scenes.visual: The two trees merge back into one full-size tree at left; the BLUE kidney receptor returns at lower right and the WHITE pituitary at top right, with all GREEN gates working and dots flowing evenly. On 'where the pathway breaks', the GREEN gates pulse; on 'the steroids left behind', the receptor pulses; on 'the feedback respond last', the WHITE ACTH arrow and the PURPLE brake arrow pulse together. On 'each level's direction', small up and down arrows flicker beside the three branch tips with no numbers, then settle; a GREY tag reads 'direction, not size'.

End card over the dimmed but still moving tree (dots flowing up the trunk into the YELLOW, PURPLE and MAGENTA branches; the BLUE receptor and WHITE pituitary faint at the edges). Large white text, centred: 'Read adrenal disease in order: enzymes, then receptors, then loops.'
